paper_metadata.title: Transient liquid phase bonding of γ′- precipitation strengthened Ni based superalloys for repairing gas turbine components

evidence.quote: ′'-Precipitation strengthened Ni based superalloys are extensively being accepted for gas turbine components
GTD111 is produced by the directional solidification (DS) process, while Udimet520 is a wrought alloy.
Rectangular coupons (10 × 10 × 5 mm) were taken from the service-exposed gas turbine blades of GTD111 and Udimet520
GTD111 is produced by the directional solidification (DS) process, while Udimet520 is a wrought alloy.
A commercial Ni–Cr-Si–B alloy (MBF-50), in the form of an amorphous foil of thickness 40 μm was used as the filler metal and its liquidus temperature was 1140 ◦C.
TLP bonding operation was carried out at 1140, 1170 and 1190 ◦C for 60, 90 and 120 min under vacuum of 1×10−2 Pa, followed by furnace cooling to 25 ◦C after the bonding finished.

Fig. 10 shows EMPA analysis result on B along the grain boundaries in a specimen of Udimet520 bonded at 1140 ◦C for 0 min.
The bright area (indicated as “A” in Fig. 2) is the dendrite core and the dark area (B) is the dendrite boundary in this material.
Udimet520, on the other hand, has a polycrystalline structure with polygonal grains.
An area with a lot of fine particles called the diffusion affected zone (DAZ) is also observed between the joint and the base metal.
The EPMA result on the DAZ shows that these precipitates are fine bulky Cr carbo-boride particles and larger needle-like Cr carbo-borides (in Fig. 6).

Fine Cr-borides and needle-like Cr-borides, which were identified in the DAZ of the GTD111 specimen, were first detected in the grains and also along the grain boundaries in the DAZ.
This result proves that the grain boundaries are the preferential path for diffusion of melting point depressing elements in these superalloys.
Consequently, this leads to the faster isothermal solidification in the joint of polycrystalline Udimet520 compared to GTD111.

If holding time is not enough for isothermal solidification to be completed, residual melted filler metal will be solidified via athermal solidification and produce brittle phases with melting point depressing elements such B and Si in the joint
